title: Parallax Auto-Bid POC: Mixed-workload latency, throughput, and cost benchmarking
body:
Executive summary:

This doc captures the benchmarking and performance evaluation we ran for the Parallax Auto-Bid POC (adtech bidder). The customer workload is mixed: a high-volume short-inference path (fast scoring, 8–64 token outputs) representing bid scoring, and a less-frequent long-inference path (policy explanation / creative rewrite, 256–1024 tokens). The goal was to measure latency distributions, achievable QPS under SLOs, and raw cost per 1M output tokens under different model/quantization/deployment configurations.

Key takeaways (short):
- Baseline (fp16, no quant) on Dedicated GPUs: short-path p95 = 28ms, p99 = 62ms at 4k concurrent short QPS with 8-token outputs.
- int8 quantized model yields ~1.6x cost improvement with modest p95 degradation (~+6ms) for short-path when KV cache is warm; p99 impact larger (+18ms) for cold-cache cases.
- Mixed workload causes tail amplification: adding 10% long requests (avg 512 tokens) increases short-path p99 by ~35% unless strict request shaping is used.
- Best cost/latency tradeoff for Parallax: Dedicated pool with two model variants + smart routing (short->quantized small model, long->fp16 full model) + aggressive KV caching and warmup scripts. Estimated unit cost ~ $0.78 per 1k output tokens for the mixed workload (x86 region pricing assumptions; detailed numbers below).

Context and success criteria:
- Customer SLO: p95 short-path <= 50ms, p99 short-path <= 120ms, throughput target 5k QPS short-path sustained during peak windows.
- Cost target: reduce inference unit cost relative to their current vendor by >= 25% while meeting latency SLOs.
- Deployment options considered: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Redwood Private (VPC), and Hosted API for quick validation. This run targeted Dedicated-like hardware (A800 equivalent GPUs, 48GB VRAM per GPU).

Test matrix (high level):
- Model variants: large-base-v1 fp16 (baseline), large-base-v1 int8 (static quant), med-smaller-v1 fp16 (reduced params for short-path).
- Cache state: cold (fresh worker, no KV), warm (prefilled KV with 1h simulated traffic), hot (continuous traffic).
- Batching config: none (streaming, batch size 1), adaptive batching (max batch 32, timeout 8ms), large batching (max batch 64, timeout 25ms).
- Routing policy: naive (first-available), workload-aware (route short to quantized/med), strict isolation (dedicated pool for long).
- Load shapes: steady short-only, mixed (90% short / 10% long), burst (sudden 10x spike for 30s).

Environment and measurement notes:
- Hardware: 4x A800-equivalent GPUs per node, 12 nodes in pool. Workers configured with 2 inference instances per GPU (per Redwood config).
- Measurement tool: internal load generator (bench-gen v2.1), measurement agents collated into a single CSV.
- Metrics captured: latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99), tokens per second, GPU utilization, GPU memory, and per-token amortized cost (using accounting export).
- All runs repeated 3 times; numbers below show representative run (median) plus variance where notable.

Detailed results: short-path baseline (fp16, warm KV, adaptive batching)
- Input profile: 4 tokens prompt, 8 tokens average output.
- Sustained QPS: 4,000 short QPS per pool (across 12 nodes).
- Latency: p50=10ms, p90=21ms, p95=28ms, p99=62ms.
- GPU utilization average: 72%.
- Cost: $1.02 per 1k output tokens (baseline accounting).

Short-path with int8 quant (static quant, warm KV)
- Same traffic shape.
- Latency: p50=12ms, p90=26ms, p95=34ms, p99=80ms.
- Observations: p95 increase ~6ms; p99 more impacted by kernel selection jitter under peak microbursts.
- Cost: $0.61 per 1k output tokens (approx 40% saving vs baseline).

Long-path baseline (512 token outputs, fp16)
- Load: 400 long QPS (10% of traffic in mixed run).
- Latency: p50=180ms, p90=420ms, p95=610ms, p99=1.2s.
- GPU utilization (mixed): 85% overall; memory pressure increases for long runs, causing occasional GC stalls measured as 3–8ms cpu-side pauses.
- Cost: $2.9 per 1k output tokens (higher due to length and memory transfers).

Mixed workload (90% short + 10% long) naive routing
- Short-path latencies inflated: p95 short = 38ms, p99 short = 105ms; short p99 > baseline by ~70%.
- Root cause: model swap and IO interference when long requests occupy worker threads and cause cache eviction; batching heuristics also coalesce dissimilar sequences producing queueing delays.

Mitigations tested and outcomes:
1) Workload-aware routing (short->quantized/med, long->fp16 full)
   - Short p95 restored to 29ms, p99=68ms. Long p95 unchanged.
   - Cost: blended $0.78 per 1k output tokens.

2) Strict isolation (separate pools)
   - Short p95=26ms, p99=60ms; long p95 improved slightly due to dedicated memory.
   - Operational cost increase: +12% capex due to lower bin-packing efficiency.

3) Aggressive KV cache warmup + prioritized cache residency
   - Reduced cold-start tail: p99 for short reduced by ~20% in burst windows. Requires warmup script executed at start of peak window (~10s per worker).

4) Adaptive batching tuning (max batch 16, timeout 6ms)
   - Best balance for short-path peak latency; large batching pushed p99 higher for short.

Cold-start and microburst behavior:
- Cold workers: short p99 exploded to 240–320ms until KV warmed. Warmup script (synthetic short-path requests) brought cold workers within 1–2s.
- Microbursts: a 10x sudden spike caused queueing; combining adaptive batching with request shaping (leaky bucket) smoothed tail; under no-shaping, p99 for short exceeded 500ms.

Operational recommendations for Parallax POC:
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated pool with two model variants (med-quant for short, fp16 full for long). Use workload-aware routing policy with a small reserved headroom for long tasks to avoid eviction during bursts.
- Autoscaling: conservative scale-up threshold (CPU/GPU queue depth) + burst capacity enabled to absorb short spikes. Scale-down with cooldown 3–5 minutes to avoid oscillation during bursty traffic.
- Warmup: schedule warmup scripts 2 min before known peaks; warmup traffic should include representative short prompts to populate KV cache.
- Batching config: adaptive batching with max_batch=16 and timeout=6ms for short-path workers; long-path workers use larger batch sizes but isolated.
- Monitoring: per-route p95/p99, KV cache hit-rate, worker churn, and per-token cost. Create alerts at p95>50ms and p99>120ms for short-path.

Cost modeling (approx):
- Baseline (single fp16 model): $1.02 per 1k tokens short-heavy workload.
- Optimized (mixed routing + quant): blended $0.78 per 1k tokens.
- Dedicated+strict isolation adds ~12% to infra cost but simplifies guarantees; still cheaper than vendor baseline in the customer comparison.

Open questions and risks:
- Quantization fidelity: we observed occasional low-confidence outputs for a small subset (~0.5%) of short scoring prompts when using int8; QA needs to run Parallax's business rules over a production prompt set.
- Failure modes: worker OOMs were rare but occurred during long-path runs with concurrent large batches; add memory margin or use lower max_batch for long workers.
- Region placement: legal requirement to keep logs in-region may force smaller pools and reduce bin-packing efficiency. Need to re-run sizing per region.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- SE: run fidelity sweep of quantized med model against Parallax 5k golden prompts and provide confusion matrix (owner: Daniel Chu, due 2029-06-20).
- Eng: prototype warmup orchestrator job that runs at peak boundaries and verify cold start improvements across 3 clusters (owner: Ravi Patel, due 2029-06-25).
- Product: propose routing UI defaults for workload-aware policies to reduce operator friction (owner: Marina López, due 2029-06-22).
- Ops: create dashboard for per-route p95/p99, KV hit-rate, and cost per 1k tokens (owner: Aisha Mendes, due 2029-06-18).

Appendix: raw sample numbers (representative run)
- Short-only (baseline fp16): QPS=4000, p50=10ms, p90=21ms, p95=28ms, p99=62ms, cost=1.02/1k
- Short-only (int8 quant): QPS=4200, p50=12ms, p90=26ms, p95=34ms, p99=80ms, cost=0.61/1k
- Mixed naive (90/10): short p95=38ms, p99=105ms; long p95=610ms
- Mixed optimized routing: short p95=29ms, p99=68ms; blended cost=0.78/1k

Notes and meeting context:
- This doc was produced after a two-day onsite workshop with Parallax engineering. Numbers above represent a controlled Dedicated-like environment; hosted API will show different numers due to multi-tenant effects.
- Refer to linked artifacts for raw CSVs and bench-gen configs.

Comments welcome — please add inline notes or push PR with updated CSV references.
